- E004: compile plus fused SGD cut time about 14% (10.55 to 9.04 s) at unchanged accuracy. E003 shows that recompile leaks inside timed code are catastrophic: +3 s.
- E005: Lookahead/EMA added +0.97 pp for about 0.06 s. The best lever per unit of budget so far.
- E006: Muon at batch 2000 added +0.66 pp (0.7583 to 0.7649) for +0.35 s (+4%). Muon is slower per epoch (Newton-Schulz) but buys about 1 epoch of accuracy, so it was worth it.
- E007: progressive resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30% cut time 22% (9.45 to 7.33 s) and cost 0.59 pp. That is 2.1 s for 0.6 pp, a much better rate than epochs.

Budget model: time ≈ F + V × (pixel-weighted epoch fraction).
- Fitting E006 and E007 gives F ≈ 0.8 s fixed (prepare H2D, eigh, pad, first-step effects) and V ≈ 8.65 s of variable time at full-res 10 epochs, so about 0.87 s per full-res epoch.

1. Narrower last group (512): about 5% of time, small accuracy cost.

structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E007. Correction carried forward: HYP epochs = 10.0, batch 2000, which gives 25 steps per epoch and 250 steps total. E005, E006 and E007 all ran at 10 epochs. Ideas that say "9 epochs" mislabel the base, so an epoch "trim to 8.5" may really be a 1.5-epoch (15%) cut.

What was measured:
- E004: compile plus fused SGD cut time about 14% (10.55 to 9.04 s) at unchanged accuracy. E003 shows that recompile leaks inside timed code are catastrophic: +3 s.
- E005: Lookahead/EMA added +0.97 pp for about 0.06 s. The best lever per unit of budget so far.
- E006: Muon at batch 2000 added +0.66 pp (0.7583 to 0.7649) for +0.35 s (+4%). Muon is slower per epoch (Newton-Schulz) but buys about 1 epoch of accuracy, so it was worth it.
- E007: progressive resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30% cut time 22% (9.45 to 7.33 s) and cost 0.59 pp. That is 2.1 s for 0.6 pp, a much better rate than epochs.

Budget model: time ≈ F + V × (pixel-weighted epoch fraction).
- Fitting E006 and E007 gives F ≈ 0.8 s fixed (prepare H2D, eigh, pad, first-step effects) and V ≈ 8.65 s of variable time at full-res 10 epochs, so about 0.87 s per full-res epoch.
- Time scales almost linearly with pixel count. Kernels at 24 px are not badly underused at batch 2000.
- Accuracy slope versus epochs is about 0.6-0.7 pp per epoch (E001/E002 measured; with EMA plus Muon it may be flatter). 1 pp costs about 1.3-1.5 s via epochs.
- Margin is 0.7590 − 0.753 = 0.60 pp, about 0.9 epoch at the slope, or about 0.65 s. A 40-seed safety bar near 0.756 leaves about 0.3 pp.

Remaining levers, ranked by expected net seconds:
1. Narrower last group (512): about 5% of time, small accuracy cost.
2. More aggressive resizing: about 0.8-1.0 s saved, but the accuracy cost probably grows faster than linearly at 20 px.
3. Epoch trim: about 0.35 s per 0.5 epoch.
4. CUDA graphs: 250 steps × a few ms of launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin is 0.3-0.8 s, but there is compile and leak risk.
5. LR-to-0 and BN recalibration: small accuracy gains (≤0.3 pp) mostly redundant with EMA. BN recalibration risks a new-shape compile or cuDNN autotune inside timed code.

Noise: compiled runs look deterministic per seed (E003 and E004 had identical accuracy). Per-seed std is probably 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Time noise is 1-2%.

My misses: I systematically underestimated the accuracy gains of EMA, Muon and resizing (three misses on the low side). I am shifting accuracy priors up by about 0.3-0.5 pp and trusting cheap levers more.

Unsure about:
- the epoch slope with Muon plus EMA;
- whether 20 px hurts much more than 24 px;
- the size of the per-step launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin;
- whether the 40-seed mean sits below the seeds 0-2 mean.

forecasts.reason: The real base is 10 epochs. A cut to 8.5 removes 15% of the variable time (about 1 s) but costs about 0.9 pp, landing near the bar. If the implementer reads it as a 0.5-epoch cut, the result is about 6.95 s and 0.756.
The end-of-run averaging from Lookahead/EMA already does most of what a zero LR floor would. Expected gain is about 0.15 pp, under the 0.3 pp bar, at zero time cost.

The pixel-weighted fraction drops from 0.755 to 0.64, saving about 0.9 s. At 20 px the accuracy cost probably grows superlinearly (about 0.8 pp), so the trade is roughly a wash against an epoch cut and likely just below 0.753.
Narrowing the last group cuts its FLOPs by about 20%, which is about 5% of the total. Muon's orthogonalized updates are width-robust, so the accuracy loss is about 0.2 pp.
The same recipe on held-out seeds should give a mean within 0.3 pp of seeds 0-2, possibly slightly lower from regression to the mean. Per-seed std should be about 0.25 pp.
250 steps × 2-4 ms of launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin could save about 0.3-0.8 s. But cudagraph plus max-autotune with Muon and per-resolution capture risks leaks, extra copies or failure.

Lookahead already averages the BN buffers, so the gain is likely ≤0.2 pp. A 5k-batch train-mode forward is a new shape, triggering cuDNN autotune or a recompile in timed code, so it likely exceeds the 0.15 s budget.

cruxes: With Muon and EMA on, how many pp does each 0.5 epoch cost? Measured from the true 10-epoch base, not 9. This sets the price of the epoch dial against resizing and width cuts.
How much of the 7.33 s is fixed or launch overhead (F ≈ 0.8 s inferred; per-step CPU launch time under the 4-CPU pin)? This decides whether CUDA graphs or prepare work beat FLOP cuts.
Is the accuracy cost of resizing linear in pixel savings, or does it jump below 24 px? This decides whether I011's schedule is a net gain.
